sanskrit: kāni rūpāṇi śakrasya bhavanty āgacchato mune vapus tejaś ca kīdṛg vai tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: What forms does Śakra assume when he comes, O sage? Of what kind is his body and his splendor? This you ought to expound to me.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhagavāṃs tasmai vipulāya mahātmane ācacakṣe yathātattvaṃ māyāṃ śakrasya bhārata
english: Then that blessed one, O Bhārata, declared to the great-souled Vipula, according to the truth, the magic art of Śakra.

sanskrit: bahumāyaḥ sa viprarṣe balahā pākaśāsanaḥ tāṃs tān vikurute bhāvān bahūn atha muhur muhuḥ
english: Rich in illusions, O brahmin-seer, is the slayer of Bala, the chastiser of Pāka; this form and that he conjures, manifold, again and again.

sanskrit: kirīṭī vajrabhṛd dhanvī mukuṭī baddhakuṇḍalaḥ bhavaty atha muhūrtena caṇḍālasamadarśanaḥ
english: Diademed, wielder of the thunderbolt, bearing a bow, crowned, with fastened earrings he appears; and in a moment he looks like a caṇḍāla.

sanskrit: śikhī jaṭī cīravāsāḥ punar bhavati putraka bṛhaccharīraś ca punaḥ pīvaro 'tha punaḥ kṛśaḥ
english: With a topknot, with matted locks, clad in bark, he becomes again, my son; now huge of body, now stout, now lean.

sanskrit: gauraṃ śyāmaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca varṇaṃ vikurute punaḥ virūpo rūpavāṃś caiva yuvā vṛddhas tathaiva ca
english: Fair, dusky, and dark of hue he becomes by turns; misshapen and again comely, young and likewise old.

sanskrit: prājño jaḍaś ca mūkaś ca hrasvo dīrghas tathaiva ca brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyaś caiva vaiśyaḥ śūdras tathaiva ca pratilomānulomaś ca bhavaty atha śatakratuḥ
english: Wise and dull and mute, short and likewise tall; a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, and likewise a śūdra, born against the grain and with it—so does the lord of a hundred sacrifices become.

sanskrit: śukavāyasarūpī ca haṃsakokilarūpavān siṃhavyāghragajānāṃ ca rūpaṃ dhārayate punaḥ
english: In the form of a parrot and a crow, in the form of a goose and a cuckoo, and again he takes on the shape of lions, tigers, and elephants.

sanskrit: daivaṃ daityam atho rājñāṃ vapur dhārayate 'pi ca sukṛśo vāyubhagnāṅgaḥ śakunir vikṛtas tathā
english: The body of a god, of a daitya, and of kings he bears as well; very lean, his limbs broken by the wind, a misshapen bird likewise.

sanskrit: catuṣpād bahurūpaś ca punar bhavati bāliśaḥ makṣikāmaśakādīnāṃ vapur dhārayate 'pi ca
english: Four-footed and of many forms he again becomes a fool; and he takes on too the body of flies, gnats, and the like.

sanskrit: na śakyam asya grahaṇaṃ kartuṃ vipula kena cit api viśvakṛtā tāta yena sṛṣṭam idaṃ jagat
english: None can lay hold of him, O Vipula—not even by the Maker of all, dear son, by whom this world was created.

sanskrit: punar antarhitaḥ śakro dṛśyate jñānacakṣuṣā vāyubhūtaś ca sa punar devarājo bhavaty uta
english: Now Śakra, hidden, is seen only by the eye of wisdom; and having become wind, that king of the gods becomes himself once more.

sanskrit: evaṃ rūpāṇi satataṃ kurute pākaśāsanaḥ tasmād vipula yatnena rakṣemāṃ tanumadhyamām
english: Thus does the chastiser of Pāka ceaselessly take on these forms; therefore, Vipula, guard with all effort this slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: yathā ruciṃ nāvalihed devendro bhṛgusattama kratāv upahitaṃ nyastaṃ haviḥ śveva durātmavān
english: See that the king of the gods does not lap up Ruci, O best of the Bhṛgus, as an evil-natured dog laps the oblation set down and placed at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: evam ākhyāya sa munir yajñakāro 'gamat tadā devaśarmā mahābhāgas tato bharatasattama
english: Having thus spoken, that sage, the performer of the sacrifice, then departed—the greatly fortunate Devaśarman, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: vipulas tu vacaḥ śrutvā guroś cintāparo 'bhavat rakṣāṃ ca paramāṃ cakre devarājān mahābalāt
english: But Vipula, having heard his teacher's word, fell to brooding, and devised the utmost guard against the king of the gods of great might.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ gurudārābhirakṣaṇe māyāvī hi surendro 'sau durdharṣaś cāpi vīryavān
english: "What can I do to guard my teacher's wife? For that lord of the gods is a master of illusion, unassailable, and mighty in valor.

sanskrit: nāpidhāyāśramaṃ śakyo rakṣituṃ pākaśāsanaḥ uṭajaṃ vā tathā hy asya nānāvidhasarūpatā
english: Not by shutting up the hermitage can the chastiser of Pāka be warded off, nor the leaf-hut, for his forms are of every kind.

sanskrit: vāyurūpeṇa vā śakro gurupatnīṃ pradharṣayet tasmād imāṃ saṃpraviśya ruciṃ sthāsye 'ham adya vai
english: In the form of the wind Śakra might assail my teacher's wife; therefore, entering into this Ruci, I shall this very day take my station within her.

sanskrit: atha vā pauruṣeṇeyam aśakyā rakṣituṃ mayā bahurūpo hi bhagavāñ chrūyate harivāhanaḥ
english: Or else by mere manly strength she cannot be guarded by me, for the blessed one borne by bays is heard to be of many forms.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ yogabalād enāṃ rakṣiṣye pākaśāsanāt gātrāṇi gātrair asyāhaṃ saṃpravekṣye 'bhirakṣitum
english: Therefore by the power of yoga I shall guard her from the chastiser of Pāka; I shall enter limb by limb into her limbs to keep her safe.

sanskrit: yady ucchiṣṭām imāṃ patnīṃ ruciṃ paśyeta me guruḥ śapsyaty asaṃśayaṃ kopād divyajñāno mahātapāḥ
english: Yet if my teacher should see this wife Ruci defiled, then beyond doubt he, of divine knowledge and great austerity, will curse me in his wrath.

sanskrit: na ceyaṃ rakṣituṃ śakyā yathānyā pramadā nṛbhiḥ māyāvī hi surendro 'sāv aho prāpto 'smi saṃśayam
english: And she cannot be guarded as other women are guarded by men, for that lord of the gods is a master of illusion—alas, I have come into peril!"

sanskrit: avaśyakaraṇīyaṃ hi guror iha hi śāsanam yadi tv etad ahaṃ kuryām āścaryaṃ syāt kṛtaṃ mayā
english: "The teacher's command must surely be carried out; yet if I were to do this, a marvel would be wrought by me.

sanskrit: yogenānupraviśyeha gurupatnyāḥ kalevaram nirmuktasya rajorūpān nāparādho bhaven mama
english: Entering by yoga here into the body of my teacher's wife, free from any form of passion, no fault would be mine.

sanskrit: yathā hi śūnyāṃ pathikaḥ sabhām adhyāvaset pathi tathādyāvāsayiṣyāmi gurupatnyāḥ kalevaram
english: As a wayfarer upon the road might lodge in an empty hall, so this day shall I lodge within my teacher's wife's body.

sanskrit: asaktaḥ padmapatrastho jalabindur yathā calaḥ evam eva śarīre 'syā nivatsyāmi samāhitaḥ
english: As a drop of water resting on a lotus leaf clings not, but trembles free, even so, composed, shall I dwell within her body."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ dharmam ālokya vedavedāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ tapaś ca vipulaṃ dṛṣṭvā guror ātmana eva ca
english: Thus having looked upon dharma and upon the Vedas and their lore in every part, and having regarded the abundant austerity of his teacher and of himself,

sanskrit: iti niścitya manasā rakṣāṃ prati sa bhārgavaḥ ātiṣṭhat paramaṃ yatnaṃ yathā tac chṛṇu pārthiva
english: having so resolved in his mind concerning the guarding, that descendant of Bhṛgu set himself to the utmost effort—hear how, O lord of earth.

sanskrit: gurupatnīm upāsīno vipulaḥ sa mahātapāḥ upāsīnām anindyāṅgīṃ kathābhiḥ samalobhayat
english: Seated beside his teacher's wife, Vipula of great austerity beguiled with stories that seated one of faultless limbs.

sanskrit: netrābhyāṃ netrayor asyā raśmīn saṃyojya raśmibhiḥ viveśa vipulaḥ kāyam ākāśaṃ pavano yathā
english: Joining with his two eyes the beams of her eyes, beam to beam, Vipula entered her body as the wind enters the sky.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣaṇenaiva vadanaṃ vadanena ca aviceṣṭann atiṣṭhad vai chāyevāntargato muniḥ
english: Mark upon mark, face within face, the sage stood unmoving, gone within her like a shadow.

sanskrit: tato viṣṭabhya vipulo gurupatnyāḥ kalevaram uvāsa rakṣaṇe yukto na ca sā tam abudhyata
english: Then Vipula, holding fast the body of his teacher's wife, abode there intent on guarding, and she was not aware of him.

sanskrit: yaṃ kālaṃ nāgato rājan gurus tasya mahātmanaḥ kratuṃ samāpya svagṛhaṃ taṃ kālaṃ so 'bhyarakṣata
english: For all the while, O king, that the great-souled teacher had not returned to his own house, his sacrifice concluded, for all that while did he keep watch.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ kadā cid devendro divyarūpavapurdharaḥ idam antaram ity evaṃ tato 'bhyāgād athāśramam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then on a certain day the king of the gods, bearing a body of divine form, thinking "this is the moment," came thereupon to the hermitage.

sanskrit: rūpam apratimaṃ kṛtvā lobhanīyaṃ janādhipa darśanīyatamo bhūtvā praviveśa tam āśramam
english: Having made for himself a peerless, alluring form, O ruler of men, becoming most fair to behold, he entered that hermitage.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tam āsīnaṃ vipulasya kalevaram niśceṣṭaṃ stabdhanayanaṃ yathālekhyagataṃ tathā
english: He beheld there, seated, the body of Vipula, motionless, with fixed and staring eyes, like a figure set down in a painting.

sanskrit: ruciṃ ca rucirāpāṅgīṃ pīnaśroṇipayodharām padmapatraviśālākṣīṃ saṃpūrṇendunibhānanām
english: And Ruci of lovely sidelong glance, full of hip and breast, wide-eyed as the petals of a lotus, her face like the full moon.

sanskrit: sā tam ālokya sahasā pratyutthātum iyeṣa ha rūpeṇa vismitā ko 'sīty atha vaktum ihecchatī
english: Seeing him, she suddenly sought to rise to greet him, amazed at his beauty, wishing then to ask, "Who are you?"

sanskrit: utthātukāmāpi satī vyatiṣṭhad vipulena sā nigṛhītā manuṣyendra na śaśāka viceṣṭitum
english: Though she wished to rise, she stayed still, held fast by Vipula, O lord of men, and could not stir.

sanskrit: tām ābabhāṣe devendraḥ sāmnā paramavalgunā tvadartham āgataṃ viddhi devendraṃ māṃ śucismite
english: The king of the gods addressed her with words most soft and winning: "Know that I, the king of the gods, have come for your sake, O bright-smiling one.

sanskrit: kliśyamānam anaṅgena tvatsaṃkalpodbhavena vai tat paryāpnuhi māṃ subhru purā kālo 'tivartate
english: Tormented by the bodiless god of love, born of longing for you—therefore accept me, fair-browed one, before the time slips away."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ śakraṃ śuśrāva vipulo muniḥ gurupatnyāḥ śarīrastho dadarśa ca surādhipam
english: Vipula the sage, dwelling within the body of his teacher's wife, heard Śakra speaking thus, and beheld the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: na śaśāka ca sā rājan pratyutthātum aninditā vaktuṃ ca nāśakad rājan viṣṭabdhā vipulena sā
english: And the blameless one could not rise, O king, nor could she speak, O king, held fast as she was by Vipula.

sanskrit: ākāraṃ gurupatnyās tu vijñāya sa bhṛgūdvahaḥ nijagrāha mahātejā yogena balavat prabho babandha yogabandhaiś ca tasyāḥ sarvendriyāṇi saḥ
english: But that scion of Bhṛgu, perceiving the bearing of his teacher's wife, restrained her—he of great splendor—forcefully by yoga, O lord, and with the bonds of yoga he bound all her senses.

sanskrit: tāṃ nirvikārāṃ dṛṣṭvā tu punar eva śacīpatiḥ uvāca vrīḍito rājaṃs tāṃ yogabalamohitām
english: Seeing her unmoved, the lord of Śacī once again, abashed, O king, spoke to her who was overcome by the power of yoga.

sanskrit: ehy ehīti tataḥ sā taṃ prativaktum iyeṣa ca sa tāṃ vācaṃ guroḥ patnyā vipulaḥ paryavartayat
english: "Come, come," he said; and then she sought to answer him, but Vipula turned aside that speech of his teacher's wife.

sanskrit: bhoḥ kim āgamane kṛtyam iti tasyāś ca niḥsṛtā vaktrāc chaśāṅkapratimād vāṇī saṃskārabhūṣitā
english: "Sir, what is the purpose of your coming?"—thus from her mouth, like unto the moon, came forth speech adorned with refinement.

sanskrit: vrīḍitā sā tu tad vākyam uktvā paravaśā tadā puraṃdaraś ca saṃtrasto babhūva vimanās tadā
english: Abashed, having spoken that word against her own will, she fell silent; and Puraṃdara then grew alarmed and dismayed.

sanskrit: sa tad vaikṛtam ālakṣya devarājo viśāṃ pate avaikṣata sahasrākṣas tadā divyena cakṣuṣā
english: Marking that strangeness, the king of the gods, O lord of peoples, the thousand-eyed one, then looked with his divine eye.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca muniṃ tasyāḥ śarīrāntaragocaram pratibimbam ivādarśe gurupatnyāḥ śarīragam
english: And he beheld the sage moving within her body, lodged in his teacher's wife's frame like a reflection in a mirror.

sanskrit: sa taṃ ghoreṇa tapasā yuktaṃ dṛṣṭvā puraṃdaraḥ prāvepata susaṃtrastaḥ śāpabhītas tadā vibho
english: Seeing him endowed with terrible austerity, Puraṃdara trembled, sorely afraid, fearing a curse then, O mighty one.

sanskrit: vimucya gurupatnīṃ tu vipulaḥ sumahātapāḥ svaṃ kalevaram āviśya śakraṃ bhītam athābravīt
english: Then Vipula of great austerity, releasing his teacher's wife, entered his own body and spoke to the frightened Śakra:

sanskrit: ajitendriya pāpātman kāmātmaka puraṃdara na ciraṃ pūjayiṣyanti devās tvāṃ mānuṣās tathā
english: "O you of unconquered senses, evil-souled, lustful Puraṃdara! Not for long shall the gods, nor men likewise, honor you.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu tad vismṛtaṃ śakra na tan manasi te sthitam gautamenāsi yan mukto bhagāṅkaparicihnitaḥ
english: Have you forgotten this, Śakra? Does it not stand in your mind—how by Gautama you were marked over with the signs of a woman's parts?

sanskrit: jāne tvāṃ bāliśamatim akṛtātmānam asthiram mayeyaṃ rakṣyate mūḍha gaccha pāpa yathāgatam
english: I know you to be childish of mind, undisciplined of self, and fickle. By me is she guarded, O fool; go, O wicked one, as you came.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tvām adya mūḍhātman daheyaṃ hi svatejasā kṛpāyamāṇas tu na te dagdhum icchāmi vāsava
english: I would this day burn you to ashes by my own splendor, O dull-souled one; yet out of compassion I do not wish to burn you, Vāsava.

sanskrit: sa ca ghoratapā dhīmān gurur me pāpacetasam dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ nirdahed adya krodhadīptena cakṣuṣā
english: And that wise teacher of mine, of terrible austerity, seeing you of wicked heart, would this day burn you utterly with an eye blazing with wrath.

sanskrit: naivaṃ tu śakra kartavyaṃ punar mānyāś ca te dvijāḥ mā gamaḥ sasutāmātyo 'tyayaṃ brahmabalārditaḥ
english: Never act thus again, Śakra; the twice-born are to be honored by you. Go not, with your sons and ministers, to ruin, stricken by the might of brahman.

sanskrit: amaro 'smīti yad buddhim etām āsthāya vartase māvamaṃsthā na tapasām asādhyaṃ nāma kiṃ cana
english: Holding to the thought, 'I am immortal,' you conduct yourself so; do not despise it—there is nothing whatsoever unattainable by austerities.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ śakro vipulasya mahātmanaḥ akiṃcid uktvā vrīḍitas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Hearing that speech of the great-souled Vipula, Śakra, saying nothing, ashamed, vanished then and there.

sanskrit: muhūrtayāte śakre tu devaśarmā mahātapāḥ kṛtvā yajñaṃ yathākāmam ājagāma svam āśramam
english: When but a moment had passed since Śakra's going, Devaśarman of great austerity, having performed his sacrifice as he wished, came home to his hermitage.

sanskrit: āgate 'tha gurau rājan vipulaḥ priyakarmakṛt rakṣitāṃ gurave bhāryāṃ nyavedayad aninditām
english: When the teacher had come, O king, Vipula, doer of welcome deeds, presented to him the blameless wife he had guarded.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca śāntātmā sa guruṃ guruvatsalaḥ vipulaḥ paryupātiṣṭhad yathāpūrvam aśaṅkitaḥ
english: And having saluted him, that tranquil-souled Vipula, devoted to his teacher, attended upon his teacher as before, untroubled.

sanskrit: viśrāntāya tatas tasmai sahāsīnāya bhāryayā nivedayām āsa tadā vipulaḥ śakrakarma tat
english: Then to him, rested and seated together with his wife, Vipula reported that deed of Śakra.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā sa munis tuṣṭo vipulasya pratāpavān babhūva śīlavṛttābhyāṃ tapasā niyamena ca
english: Hearing this, that majestic sage grew pleased with Vipula for his character and conduct, his austerity and his self-restraint.

sanskrit: vipulasya gurau vṛttiṃ bhaktim ātmani ca prabhuḥ dharme ca sthiratāṃ dṛṣṭvā sādhu sādhv ity uvāca ha
english: Seeing Vipula's conduct toward his teacher, his devotion to him, and his steadfastness in dharma, the lord said, "Well done, well done!"

sanskrit: pratinandya ca dharmātmā śiṣyaṃ dharmaparāyaṇam vareṇa cchandayām āsa sa tasmād guruvatsalaḥ anujñātaś ca guruṇā cacārānuttamaṃ tapaḥ
english: And the righteous one, applauding his disciple who was devoted to dharma, offered to gratify him with a boon; and he, devoted to his teacher and so permitted by him, practiced unsurpassed austerity.

sanskrit: tathaiva devaśarmāpi sabhāryaḥ sa mahātapāḥ nirbhayo balavṛtraghnāc cacāra vijane vane
english: So too Devaśarman of great austerity, together with his wife, fearless of the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, roamed in the lonely forest.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vipulas tv akarot tīvraṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā guror vacaḥ tapoyuktam athātmānam amanyata ca vīryavān
english: Bhīṣma said: But Vipula, having done his teacher's bidding, performed fierce austerity; and the valiant one then deemed himself accomplished in austerity.

sanskrit: sa tena karmaṇā spardhan pṛthivīṃ pṛthivīpate cacāra gatabhīḥ prīto labdhakīrtir varo nṛṣu
english: Vying through that deed with the earth itself, O lord of earth, he roamed fearless and content, having won renown, foremost among men.

sanskrit: ubhau lokau jitau cāpi tathaivāmanyata prabhuḥ karmaṇā tena kauravya tapasā vipulena ca
english: And the lord deemed that both worlds had been won by him likewise, O Kaurava, through that deed and through his abundant austerity.

sanskrit: atha kāle vyatikrānte kasmiṃś cit kurunandana rucyā bhaginyā dānaṃ vai babhūva dhanadhānyavat
english: Then when some time had passed, O delight of the Kurus, there was a giving in marriage of Ruci's sister, with wealth and grain.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu divyā kā cid varāṅganā bibhratī paramaṃ rūpaṃ jagāmātha vihāyasā
english: At that very time a certain divine and lovely woman, bearing surpassing beauty, passed through the air.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ śarīrāt puṣpāṇi patitāni mahītale tasyāśramasyāvidūre divyagandhāni bhārata
english: From her body flowers fell to the earth, not far from that hermitage, fragrant with a divine scent, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāny agṛhṇāt tato rājan rucir nalinalocanā tadā nimantrakas tasyā aṅgebhyaḥ kṣipram āgamat
english: These then Ruci of lotus eyes gathered up, O king; and just then a summoner came swiftly on her sister's behalf.

sanskrit: tasyā hi bhaginī tāta jyeṣṭhā nāmnā prabhāvatī bhāryā citrarathasyātha babhūvāṅgeśvarasya vai
english: For her elder sister, dear son, Prabhāvatī by name, had become the wife of Citraratha, the lord of the Aṅgas.

sanskrit: pinahya tāni puṣpāṇi keśeṣu varavarṇinī āmantritā tato 'gacchad rucir aṅgapater gṛhān
english: Having bound those flowers in her hair, the fair-complexioned one, being invited, then went, that Ruci, to the house of the lord of the Aṅgas.

sanskrit: puṣpāṇi tāni dṛṣṭvātha tadāṅgendravarāṅganā bhaginīṃ codayām āsa puṣpārthe cārulocanā
english: Seeing those flowers, the lovely consort of the Aṅga lord, the fair-eyed one, then urged her sister to obtain such flowers.

sanskrit: sā bhartre sarvam ācaṣṭa ruciḥ surucirānanā bhaginyā bhāṣitaṃ sarvam ṛṣis tac cābhyanandata
english: Ruci of most lovely face told all to her husband; and the sage approved of all that had been spoken by her sister.
